text:
I built a thing for when you're stuck at a red light.

Everyone around you who has it open shows up. No names, no accounts. You're just your car. Red Car, Blue SUV, White Van.

You type, everyone within a few hundred metres sees it. Nothing is saved.
replies:
It's a single web page, nothing to install: https://meelie24.github.io/daily/traffic/

Typing locks itself while you're moving, so it's a red-light and traffic-jam thing rather than a driving thing.
The catch with proximity chat is being the only one there. So there's one room at 19:00 UTC every day that ignores location completely. Turn up then and there will be other people in it.

text:
How the proximity bit works, since a few people asked.

Your position becomes a geohash, and the geohash is the chat room. You publish to your own square and listen to the eight around it, so two cars either side of a boundary still find each other.
replies:
Coordinates get rounded to about 55 m before they go out, and your handle changes every time you cross a square, so nobody watching the relay can stitch your heartbeats into a whole trip.

It's one HTML file: https://meelie24.github.io/daily/traffic/

text:
One thing it deliberately won't do: tell you which direction anyone is in.

"The blue car behind you" plus anonymity is a targeting reticle, and everyone involved can physically see each other. You get coarse distance and nothing else.
replies:
Same reason there are no replies, no DMs and no mentions. It's broadcast to the area or nothing.

https://meelie24.github.io/daily/traffic/
